nonStandardPatterns.whatItDoes: The entire hub is rendered TWICE inside <main> — a desktop version (a real <table>) and a mobile version (a card layout built from govuk-grid-row divs with govuk-label--s spans and govuk-section-break rules). CSS shows one and hides the other by viewport. Buttons/links are duplicated with -mobile / -desktop id suffixes.
nonStandardPatterns.concern: Two full copies of the same form and its submit buttons means duplicated markup, duplicated ids, and two POST targets to keep in sync. The rebuild should render the transporter list once and rely on a single responsive component.
nonStandardPatterns.govukAlternative: GOV.UK Table is responsive on its own; or use a Summary list / Summary card per transporter (label:value pairs) which reflows to mobile without a second markup tree.

nonStandardPatterns.whatItDoes: In the mobile form the class govuk-table is put on a plain <div> and the rows are govuk-grid-row divs — the Table component's visual class reused on non-table markup.
nonStandardPatterns.concern: Non-semantic use of the table class; not how the Design System intends govuk-table to be used.
nonStandardPatterns.govukAlternative: Summary list (govuk-summary-list) for the label:value card layout.

nonStandardPatterns.whatItDoes: Custom wrapper div around the desktop <table>, presumably enabling horizontal scroll / responsive behaviour.
nonStandardPatterns.concern: Bespoke class, not part of govuk-frontend.
nonStandardPatterns.govukAlternative: Wrap wide tables in an overflow-x:auto container using govuk utilities, or rely on the responsive table pattern.

nonStandardPatterns.concern: Custom CSS utility; not a govuk class.
nonStandardPatterns.govukAlternative: govuk-frontend has no direct equivalent; a small project utility class is acceptable, or govuk-!- spacing utilities where possible.

fields.name: add-transporter-from-bip
fields.label: Add a transporter

fields.conditionalOn: Empty state only — the 'Add a transporter' link is present when no transporter has been added; once one exists the row instead shows a 'Change' link and no add link is rendered.
fields.evidence: trace 94d29a163f6ab37556cd585b4eabeec9b9c27d84 action 112 (link present, empty table) vs action 125 (link absent, one row + 'Change'). NB control is a hyperlink, not an input; navigates to /transport/transporter/search. QA locator: page-objects/notification/TransporterPage.ts:6-8. The CHED-P workflow clicks it from the initial page, creates and confirms a transporter, returns here and then continues: workflows/notification/ched-p-workflows.ts:503-517.

validationMessages.trigger: This hub was only exercised in a passing happy-path trace (0 errors). Whether a transporter is mandatory (e.g. an error if you Save and continue with no transporter) was not exercised.
validationMessages.evidence: trace 94d29a163f6ab37556cd585b4eabeec9b9c27d84 — no govuk-error-summary rendered on this page. The CHED-P workflow always adds and confirms a transporter before returning and clicking Save and continue (workflows/notification/ched-p-workflows.ts:503-517), so QA does not exercise the empty submission.

openQuestions: Authorised legacy source resolves the empty-submit question for the old system: this page has no page-level validator, its POST performs a no-op update, and PartOne.transporter is not @NotNull for the CVEDP transporter-details validation group (transport.js:29-47; PartOne.java:461-482). A transporter was therefore not enforced on this page for CHED-P; whether the rebuild should retain that policy is an explicit product decision.

The shared page-object-only 'No' radio and 'Select' button do not appear anywhere in the authorised CHED-P transporter template or its mobile/desktop partials (transport.html:12-25; transporterTableMobile.html:1-97; transporterTableDesktop.html:1-22). Keep them documented as inferred cross-CHED artefacts, not CHED-P requirements.

Is at least one transporter mandatory? The empty state offers 'Save and continue', but neither the trace nor QA exercises it without a transporter. The CHED-P workflow always follows Add -> create -> confirm before clicking Save and continue (workflows/notification/ched-p-workflows.ts:503-517), so mandatory-ness and exact validation copy remain gaps.

The observed journey added exactly one transporter and the 'Add a transporter' link then disappeared (replaced by a per-row 'Change' link). Confirm whether the hub is single-transporter-only or whether multiple transporters can be added (would the add link reappear? does the table grow rows?).
'Approval number' column was blank for a 'private transporter'. Confirm when an approval number is captured/displayed (likely only for approved/authorised transporter types).
'Type' showed 'private transporter'. The full set of transporter types is defined on the transporter search/create page, not this hub.
No back link was present in <main>; confirm whether IPAFFS renders a back link in page chrome for this hub.

The shared Transporter page object exposes a 'No' radio and a 'Select' button (page-objects/notification/TransporterPage.ts:9-14), neither rendered in the CHED-P trace nor used by CHED-P workflows/tests. 'Select' is used by CHED-A (workflows/notification/ched-a-workflows.ts:435). Confirm whether either control belongs to a live CHED-P transporter variant; their parent question/row semantics are otherwise unknown.
